product_overview: Sepolia ETH Faucet is a Next.js 14 web application designed to securely provide free Sepolia testnet ETH to Ethereum developers, testers, and blockchain learners. It integrates a backend wallet for direct ETH transfers combined with multi-layer security, including rate limiting and ad verification, ensuring reliable and abuse-resistant distribution of testnet funds.
core_goals: Provide a secure and reliable source of Sepolia ETH for development and testing purposes.
Integrate Web3 wallet connections supporting popular wallets like MetaMask and Coinbase Wallet.
Implement an interactive ad verification system to prevent abuse and ensure user engagement.
Enforce multi-layer rate limiting based on IP address and wallet address to protect the faucet.
Display real-time faucet wallet balance and transaction statuses to users.
Ensure seamless error handling and graceful UI feedback for failures and loading states.
Demonstrate best practices in security, architecture, and usability for Ethereum faucets.
key_features: Direct ETH Transfers from a backend wallet using ethers.js and environment-secured private keys.
Web3 Wallet Connection supporting injected wallets with error handling and loading indicators.
Ad Verification System with a 10-second interactive ad timer and server-side session verification to prevent abuse.
Multi-layer Rate Limiting combining IP address and wallet address restrictions to regulate ETH claims.
Real-time Faucet Statistics API providing live balance and operational status updates for the faucet wallet.
Token Claim Interface displaying user balance, transaction progress, and error states.
Comprehensive Error Handling with error boundaries and loading spinners for user-friendly UI feedback.
Context-based State Management using React Context to manage faucet state and API interactions.
Responsive and aesthetic UI styled with Tailwind CSS including custom gradients and accessible patterns.
Debug Tools available for monitoring wallet connections and ad verification sessions during development.
user_flow_summary: User visits the main faucet page and connects their preferred Web3 wallet via WalletConnect component.
The user is prompted to view an interactive advertisement which runs a 10-second timer enforcing ad engagement.
Upon successful ad viewing, the backend verifies the ad session to confirm eligibility.
User submits a claim request for Sepolia ETH which triggers backend transfer after validation of rate limits and input.
User views transaction status, with links to Etherscan for verification and balance updates reflected in the UI.
If the user attempts multiple requests too frequently, rate limiting prevents further claims until cooldown expires.
Any errors in wallet connection, ad verification, or ETH transfer are caught and displayed gracefully using error boundaries.
Users can debug and verify session states during development via dedicated debug tools.
The faucet wallet balance and operational health are accessible via the faucet statistics API shown on the frontend.
validation_criteria: Successful connection to supported Web3 wallets with error and loading state feedback.
Ad verification process enforces a full 10-second viewing timer and rejects premature aborts.
Backend securely sends ETH to user wallets respecting environment variable-defined limits.
Rate limiting prevents multiple claims from the same IP or wallet address within the cooldown period.
Frontend reflects real-time faucet balance and transaction statuses accurately.
Error boundaries catch and display all runtime errors without crashing the UI.
API endpoints validate all inputs and return consistent, informative error responses on failure.
Performance and responsiveness meet standards across desktop and mobile devices.
All environment variables and secrets are securely managed and not exposed to the frontend.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests cover frontend components and backend API routes to ensure reliability.
